meta.title: Mana Dorks Is Back! | Commander Gameplay | Episode 1
meta.format: Commander (EDH), 4-player, 40 life - played on a DIGITAL VIRTUAL TABLETOP (see platform_analysis)

result.attribution_correction: Initially misattributed to N3cro from audio alone; the published decklists settled it - the mega-turn's exclusive cards (Sunbird's Invocation, Gratuitous Violence, Archetype of Aggression, Hammer of Purphoros, Nalfeshnee, Delayed Blast Fireball) appear ONLY in Dnide's list. Decklists as ground truth.
result.finish: Mega-turn ~1:21-1:37: Wild-Magic Sorcerer/cascade chains into Gratuitous Violence + Archetype of Aggression + Hammer of Purphoros + Unnatural Growth; commander swings for 12 doubled to 24 commander damage ('that's a one shot'); NanMan's dying Vraska's Fall hands out poison counters; table dead ~1:38:17

meta.note: FIRST game in the dataset with full published decklists - convertible to .dck via engine/convert_decklist.py for replay-in-Forge conformance testing. Also first digital-tabletop game and first poison-counter finish.

sim_replay.agreement: Sim winner distribution matches the human outcome (Wildsear won both); avg sim game length 36.2 player-turns (~9 cycles) vs ~9-10 cycles in the human game; divergences: AI never assembles the one-turn Gratuitous Violence kill (wins on grind instead), poison relevant in 16/20 sims vs symbolic in the human game, and the AI pilots Siona's aura-voltron plan far below human level (commander median cast: player-turn 13, uncast in 3 games)

meta.extraction_method: YouTube auto-generated captions (ASR, unlabeled), keyword-prefiltered. Player attribution partly inferred; decklist links are authoritative for card identities.

platform_analysis.question: What system are they playing on?
evidence: 16:49 'I clicked the mountain. Did it open up a new town?' - cards are clicked, not physical
50:44 'there's a move top X cards and you just select graveyard' - zone-manipulation context menu (used for Sword of Body and Mind's mill 10)
26:04 'I got to make a wolf. Let's find a cool wolf' - token creation dialog with art search
19:59 'There is a commander damage option' - built-in life/commander-damage tracker
4:52 'people watching at home have perfect information of my hand' - hands rendered on stream
Triggers are missed and taken back freely; no game-rule enforcement anywhere - NOT a rules engine (not Arena/Forge/XMage), a free-form virtual tabletop
platform_analysis.verdict: A rules-free virtual tabletop with deck import (their Moxfield/Archidekt lists), click-to-move cards, token art picker, and integrated commander-damage tracking. Most consistent with Tabletop Simulator (MTG mod) or Cockatrice; the menu wording ('move top X cards', token dialog) matches both. NOT SpellTable (no physical cards on camera). Confidence: medium - one look at a gameplay frame settles it instantly.
platform_analysis.relevance_to_project: Whatever the tool, the format is instructive for the front-end: deck-import from Moxfield, free-form zone manipulation, and human rules-keeping - the exact opposite end of the spectrum from the Forge engine (full enforcement). A product can sit between: free-form play + the rules RAG adjudicating on demand.

key_events.detail: Turn order: NanMan (Woodland Cemetery) -> N3cro (Forest + Fyndhorn Elves - 'not the classic Manador') -> Dnide -> Shelly
Creature spells can't be countered; nontoken creatures get riot (counter or haste) - engine piece for the whole game
Enchantment mana dork - taps for X = enchantments controlled
3/3 first strike deathtouch; combat damage -> modal value
Riot gives haste, attacks Dnide immediately - commander damage tracked in the app (13:07 'that was commander damage, by the way')
'I understand that I am on the enchantment deck' - threat-assessed removal; 3/3 Beast given
Destroys Rhythm of the Wild (his own? no - targets: Rhythm...(see 21:04) + Necro's Sol Ring + commander + dual land - ATTRIBUTION MUDDY; Decimate requires four DIFFERENT targets all present
Sword protection: pro-green equipped attacker - 'he has protection from green... you CAN block it [with white/other creatures]' - protection restricts blocks only by the named quality
Serra Paragon P/T recount: 'it has the enchantment ART so you expect it to be an enchantment, but it's not' - 6/7 corrected to 5/6; card-type discipline

TRIGGER ORDERING: Noxious Newt(?) enters; player stacks Rhythm of the Wild riot counter BEFORE Tribute to the World Tree check so power stays under 3 for the two +1/+1 counters - 'so I can stack these triggers properly.' Controller orders own simultaneous triggers
2 damage to each opponent's first noncreature spell each turn - table reminds each other consistently
Connect -> wolf token + defender mills 20 (double via Felix Five Boots' trigger doubling); digital 'move top X to graveyard' used

DATASET FIRST: player CHOOSES to put commander in the GRAVEYARD instead of command zone ('I'm going to put my commander in the graveyard') - 903.9 replacement is optional; later returns it with a graveyard-recursion spell (1:06:15). Correct and strategic

CASCADE CLUSTER: definition recited; 1:03:19 'you MAY cast it'; 1:21:19 'cascade spells are exiled - they are CAST FROM EXILE' (fuels copy-on-cast-from-exile synergies); 1:23:36 tracking which casts are from exile vs hand
Commander becomes a 3/3 Frog Lizard token trade - 'frizzard'; removal by transformation

key_events.card: Gratuitous Violence (+ Archetype of Aggression, Hammer of Purphoros, Unnatural Growth, Purphoros)
key_events.detail: Damage doubling + all-trample + haste + power doubling assembled in one cascade-chain turn

Copy of legendary spell cast from exile: 'I copy it, but it's legendary so that doesn't matter' - copy enters, legend rule kills one, BUT its ETB still triggered Purphoros ('Purphoros is going to see [a creature enter] and trigger... 2 doubled to 4 damage each opponent'). Subtle and handled correctly
'He has to go down to max hand size' - cleanup discard acknowledged (correctly, unlike game_001's table)
'This is 12 and he deals double, so it's 24 for whoever I swing my commander at - that's a one shot' - 21+ commander damage kill referenced implicitly
Dying act: each opponent sacrifices + gets a POISON counter - first poison counters in the dataset (10 needed to kill; symbolic here)

N3CRO WINS. Postgame: play-of-the-game voted the early Glissa removal; 'the most important play was made in the first couple turns'; winner reveals foretold Delayed Blast Fireball contingency vs Shelly's never-cast Austere Command
'You going to remember your trigger this time?' - missed triggers ribbed, taken back freely; casual REL, human rules-keeping on a digital table
